Bachelor’s degree or foreign equivalent in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Data Science, Information Systems, or a closely related technical or quantitative field involving substantial coursework in Engineering.
Experience: 2+ years in an infrastructure, SRE, operations, DevOps, or technical-support role — or equivalent experience from a computer-science (or related) degree, a bootcamp, or substantial personal/open-source projects. We hire on demonstrated ability, not credentials.
Scripting: Comfortable scripting in at least one of Python, Bash, or Go, and eager to use code to eliminate repetitive work.
Systems foundation: Experience with Linux, containers, and at least one major public cloud (GCP, AWS, or Azure); infrastructure-as-code (Terraform) is a must.
Able to drive well-scoped problems to resolution, and to recognize when to pull in a more senior teammate.
Strong written and verbal communication and a service mindset — you communicate effectively with our internal customers.
A genuine desire to help people and unblock them — you take satisfaction in solving someone else's problem, not just your own.
Patience and composure under pressure, with the ability to stay positive and constructive.
Comfortable with a support-driven, high-context-switching, and sometimes repetitive workload — you can hold several small threads at once without losing the plot, and you drive the automation of recurring patterns.
Aim to make yourself unnecessary — automate everything to free time for larger infrastructure projects at the edges of other infrastructure pillars. We have much ground to cover.
Preferred
Exposure to CI/CD systems (GitHub Actions, Argo, or similar) and observability

Flexcompute is a cutting-edge technology startup that specializes in ultra-fast simulation technology. Our customer base includes both household names and startups in emerging industries. Our company was founded by world-renowned leaders in simulation technology from Stanford University and MIT. Tidy3D is a GPU-accelerated electromagnetic simulation product delivered as a cloud service. Behind the solver sits the platform that makes everything work: the Python client, the API, the job submission and scheduling layer, and the web application.
We are hiring a Software Engineer for the Tidy3D infrastructure team to own that platform. You will build new capability, keep the existing system healthy, and run the release and deployment process.
Responsibilities
Design and build backend services for the Tidy3D platform.
Develop and operate the control plane: the APIs, services, and data model behind task submission, job state, and result delivery.
Build scheduling and resource management for simulation jobs across heterogeneous GPU capacity.
Handle the operational concerns that come with a multi-tenant product: authentication, authorization, usage metering, and quota enforcement.
Help with the deployment of our products to customers.
Manage packaging and release to PyPI, and keep client and backend versions compatible across a long tail of installed versions.
Own the release pipeline end to end: versioning, CI/CD, staged rollout, and rollback.
Standardize deployment patterns so the same product ships to our cloud, to customer-managed cloud accounts, and to on-premises installations.

About Beyond the Game Health
Beyond the Game Health (BTGH) is a sports-health company connecting athletes, healthcare organizations, brands and communities to turn athlete influence into measurable health engagement and outcomes.
BTGH works at the intersection of sports, healthcare, technology, community engagement and athlete-powered storytelling.
We are currently developing
BTGH OS™: The Operating System for Athlete-Powered Health Engagement
, a technology platform designed to connect athletes, health organizations, brands, events and communities through measurable engagement.
What We're Building
We are moving BTGH OS from product concept and mockups into its first functional MVP.
The first release is intentionally focused. We are not trying to build the entire vision at once.
The MVP needs to demonstrate a working journey where an athlete, event or campaign can connect a user with relevant health content, drive a measurable action, and provide partners with visibility into engagement and outcomes.
The initial product thesis is:
Athlete + Event + Health Content → User Engagement → Measurable Action → Partner Analytics
For example, someone attending a BTGH event might engage with an athlete-led health campaign, access educational content, take a specific action such as completing a screening, requesting a resource or registering for a program, and generate measurable engagement data that can be surfaced to the participating health or brand partner.
This MVP will be tested through real BTGH events and campaigns and used in demonstrations, partner conversations and fundraising as we continue building toward the broader BTGH OS vision.
What You'll Work On
We're looking for a technically strong, execution-oriented intern who can work alongside our existing team to help build and deploy the first functional version of BTGH OS.
Responsibilities may include:
Translating existing product concepts, workflows and mockups into functional product features
Developing responsive web-based user experiences for athletes, consumers/patients and partners
Building front-end and back-end functionality for the MVP
Creating athlete, event, campaign and health-content profiles
Developing user engagement and action-tracking capabilities
Building QR/link-based campaign journeys that can connect physical events and athlete content to digital experiences
Creating forms, calls-to-action and workflows that capture measurable user actions
Developing basic partner-facing dashboards showing campaign engagement and outcomes
Building and maintaining databases and APIs

Testing, debugging and documenting the platform

Working with the product team to prioritize what must be built now versus what belongs on the longer-term roadmap
Considering privacy, security and responsible data collection as health-related functionality evolves
What the First MVP Needs to Prove
Success is not measured by how many features we can build.
The first release should demonstrate that BTGH can create a measurable digital journey connecting:
Athlete + Event + Health Content → User Engagement → Measurable Action → Partner Analytics
That means we need to be able to answer questions such as:
Who engaged? What content or athlete drove the engagement? What action did the user take? Which event or campaign generated it? What can we responsibly report back to the participating partner?
The MVP should be functional enough to deploy in a real BTGH activation, collect meaningful engagement data and demonstrate the product to prospective healthcare partners, sponsors and investors.

Ranking and retrieval models. Iterate the model architectures that carry the funnel: multi-task and multi-objective learning from click through conversion and GMV; multi-scenario, multi-format joint modelling; and the sample, label, and debiasing design that decides what the model actually learns.

Design and implement statistical methodologies that improve the representativeness, stability, and quality of Numerator’s products.

Contribute throughout the project lifecycle, from problem definition and exploration through implementation, testing, deployment, and ongoing evaluation.

With over $70 billion in assets, our success is driven by a culture of innovation, collaboration, and impact. We go beyond the bid—empowering our people to thrive and shape the future of the industry
About The Role
We run one of the largest digital marketplaces in residential real estate, where buyers, sellers, servicers, and agents transact on real property with real money at stake. Every listing that moves through our platform touches valuation, bidding, contracts, payments, and a long list of external systems, and the platform keeps evolving to meet the needs of the market.
We’re hiring full stack engineers to build that platform. You’ll work in React and TypeScript on the front end, Node, Kotlin, and GraphQL services behind it, running on AWS and Kubernetes. You’ll own features end to end: design, build, test, ship, and support them in production.
What The Work Looks Like
You’ll work in a lean technology org (~50 engineers) which means there is no layer between you and the work that matters. What you build ships.
You’ll ship customer-facing features and the services that power them, usually in slices small enough to get in front of users quickly.
You’ll test what you build. That means automated coverage at the unit, integration, API, and end-to-end levels, wired into CI so it keeps working after you move on. We don’t hand code to someone else to verify.
You’ll debug real problems in production. Distributed systems fail in interesting ways, and figuring out why is part of the job, not an interruption to it.
You’ll be in design discussions and code reviews as a participant, not an observer. If you think an approach is wrong, we want to hear it early.
You’ll work directly with product, UX, data, and other engineers. Most of the interesting decisions happen in those conversations.
You’ll have room to build AI-enabled features. We’re actively putting LLMs into customer and internal workflows, and engineers here are shaping what that looks like.
Who Does Well Here
The technical bar matters, but these are the traits that actually predict who thrives on this team.
You get curious when something doesn’t add up.
A weird log line, a metric that moved for no reason, a function nobody can explain. You go find out why instead of routing around it.
Blockers are problems, not stop signs.
Everyone gets stuck. What matters is what you do in the next hour. You try a few angles, read the source, check the logs, and when you do ask for help you show up with what you’ve already ruled out.
You’re still learning.
You picked up something new in the last few months, probably because you wanted to rather than because someone assigned it. You can also say “I don’t know” without it costing you anything.
You care whether it worked.
Not whether the ticket closed, whether the customer’s problem is actually solved.
What You Bring
Roughly 3+ years building and shipping production software
React, or another modern component framework you can translate from
Node.js or Kotlin/Java backend services, with REST or GraphQL APIs
Hands-on experience in AWS or a comparable cloud
Enough comfort with Docker and Kubernetes that a container deployment isn’t a black box
Automated testing as a habit rather than a phase

Where AI Meets Medicine: Build the Future of Drug Discovery in the Heart of Silicon Valley!
Making medicine that’s never been made means doing what’s never been done. About The Lilly And NVIDIA Partnership
Lilly and NVIDIA are launching a new AI co-innovation lab in the heart of Silicon Valley — an up-to-$1 billion, multi-year commitment to solve drug discovery’s toughest challenges. The lab brings Lilly scientists, technologists, chemists and biologists together with NVIDIA engineers under one roof. Together, we are building purpose-built foundation and frontier AI models trained on Lilly data at scale, tightening the feedback loop between automated wet labs and computational dry labs, designing the next generation of medicines for millions of patients across the globe.
What You’ll Be Doing
As a Data Engineer, you will build and maintain the data platforms that power AI-driven research and discovery. You will develop scalable pipelines that ingest, transform, and deliver chemical, biological, and experimental data for machine learning and scientific workflows. Partnering with AI Scientists, AI Engineers, and laboratory researchers, you will ensure that data is accurate, traceable, and accessible at scale. Your work will provide the trusted data foundation behind next-generation AI models and experiments.
How You’ll Succeed
Engineer datasets in large language environment for model training specifically efficient formats and storage layout (Parquet, Zarr, Arrow) and delivery fast enough that GPU clusters are never left waiting on data.
Design, develop, and maintain scalable and efficient data pipelines to support data analytics, reporting, and machine learning initiatives.
Ensure seamless data flow between systems and applications, optimizing data transfer and transformation processes for performance and scalability.
Build the ingestion path from the automated lab, so experimental results reach the models in hours rather than weeks, closing the loop between what a model proposes and what the next model learns from.
Own the correctness of what models train on completeness, sound joins across experimental sources, and validation that catches a bad dataset before it reaches a training run rather than after.
Build dataset versioning, lineage, and reproducibility into the platform, so any model can be traced to the exact data it was trained on months or years later.
Work with the laboratory, instrument, and external teams producing the data so that a change upstream does not quietly corrupt a training run downstream.
What You Should Bring
Strong Python, or equivalent experience building data-intensive software systems.
Strong SQL and data modeling experience including designing schemas that hold up as scientific data grows and diversifies, with expert knowledge of Postgres or a comparable enterprise database.
Distributed data processing (Spark, Ray, or Dask) and pipeline orchestration (Airflow or Dagster) at scale.
Experience with cloud platforms — AWS and Azure preferred — and with high-performance and object storage feeding large-scale compute environments.
A track record of building data systems that other people depend on, and of taking responsibility for them when they broke.
Strong testing practices and test automation, with solid CI/CD and Git fundamentals.
Adaptability and a collaborative mindset, with the ability to translate complex scientific questions into data solutions that accelerate experimentation and decision-making.
Experience streaming and event-driven integration (Kafka, MQTT, or AMQP), including instrument and laboratory data capture.
Cheminformatics or scientific data experience — compound registration, structure notation (SMILES, InChI, HELM), RDKit, multi-omics, assay, or sequencing data — is a strong plus.
Prior experience across the following: data modeling, ETL/ELT at scale, ontology development, semantic graph construction and linked data, or relational schema design.
Experience standing up, migrating, or consolidating databases and data platforms, including production cutover of systems in active use.

5+ years of data engineering experience building and operating production data systems.

Diagnose production issues from raw logs and telemetry, building observability into every system you ship so problems surface before they cascade.

Experience supporting cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, or GCP) and on-premises GPU infrastructure.
Knowledge of observability and operational monitoring, including metrics, logging, tracing, and performance tuning.

Ability to collaborate effectively with research scientists, AI engineers, and infrastructure teams in a fast-paced environment.

Responsibilities
Design, develop, and maintain software applications that support complex equipment in automated factory settings.
Write clean, efficient, and well-structured code using C#, .NET, and object-oriented programming principles.
Modify and update existing code to resolve issues, fix defects, and improve application stability.

Work with SQL and MariaDB databases to design, query, and manage data for production systems.
Use Visual Studio and related tools to build, debug, and test software solutions.

Practical experience working with SQL and MariaDB databases, including querying and data management.
Ability to use Visual Studio for coding, debugging, and testing applications.
Capability to write, modify, and optimize code for complex equipment in automated factory settings.
Skill in integrating software with new hardware and control systems.

Experience working in environments that involve automated factory equipment or industrial automation.
Comfort collaborating within a small development team and contributing to shared technical solutions.
Strong problem-solving skills and attention to detail when diagnosing and resolving software issues.
Ability to adapt to changing requirements and travel needs related to project and site support.

Approved pages and features launch on time, with the design preserved across agreed devices and browsers.
Forms, content, integrations, and key user journeys are tested; technical issues are prioritized and communicated clearly.

A meticulous, practical builder who cares about the finished interface as much as the implementation behind it.

Build + Content Management: Implement responsive pages, reusable components, content-management structures, and scoped interactions from approved designs and content.

Experience with CMS architecture, responsive design, practical testing, and clear communication across website builds and ongoing improvements.

Experience delivering websites for different brands.
E-commerce, membership, or third-party integration experience.
Technical SEO, redirects, analytics implementation, or accessible interface development.
Experience working with designers and translating detailed layouts into maintainable sites.
TOOLS YOU’LL USE
Webflow and/or Wix Studio; HTML/CSS/JavaScript; Git where custom code requires it. Use only the platform, hosting, and integrations approved for each assignment.
Figma or equivalent design references; Asana, Slack, Dropbox, and approved collaboration tools.

Engagement + Scope: Nonexclusive freelance contract. Start with one brand and agreed deliverables, milestones, and collaboration windows. Initial term and renewals are agreed in writing. Additional work may be agreed based on delivery, capacity, and mutual fit.
Location: New York City or Los Angeles; remote work within those locations or an agreed hybrid arrangement. Collaboration and any in-person meetings are agreed for each engagement.
Works with: The designated company lead and any assigned creative collaborators. This is a hands-on individual-contributor role.
Fees: US$60–$90/hour for paid discovery, scoping, and authorized hourly support, based on experience and implementation capability. Are you passionate about the art and science of testing high-precision analog and mixed-signal electronics? Do you excel at both creating robust automated test solutions and providing expert-level technical support?
Dataforth Corporation is a global leader in high-performance signal conditioning, data acquisition, and data communication products for demanding industrial markets. We are looking for a talented and motivated engineer to join our team in Tucson, AZ. This unique, dual-focus role is critical to our success, blending hands-on test development with direct customer and product support. You will not only ensure our products meet the highest standards of quality but also become a key technical resource for the products you help bring to life.
Our collaborative environment and on-site manufacturing facility mean you see the immediate impact of your work, from initial design to production and customer implementation.
How You'll Make an Impact
This is a dynamic role with two core functions:
1. Advanced Test System Development:
Develop Robust Test Solutions:
Take the lead in designing, building, and deploying automated test systems for our diverse portfolio of analog and mixed-signal products. This includes everything from PCB-level fixture design to complete system integration with custom enclosures and safety interlocks.
Create Intelligent Test Software:
Write and maintain sophisticated test software using LabVIEW, Python, or C#/C++. Your code will manage instrument control, implement complex test sequences, communicate with devices via SPI, I2C, and UART, and handle comprehensive data logging to our databases.
Drive Innovation:
Be the test engineering lead for next-generation products, ensuring our testing capabilities evolve with our cutting-edge analog and data acquisition technology.
Enhance Existing Systems:
Continuously improve and maintain current test hardware and software across all manufacturing lines to maximize uptime, precision, and efficiency.
2. Product and Customer Application Support:
Become the Product Expert:
Develop a deep technical understanding of Dataforth's entire product line, from our SCM5B signal conditioning modules to the MAQ20 data acquisition system.
Provide Tier-3 Technical Support:
Serve as the go-to engineering expert for complex customer issues escalated by our support team. Troubleshoot applications, analyze data, and help customers successfully integrate our products into critical industrial and SCADA systems.
Collaborate for Quality:
Work closely with design engineering to identify the root cause of product issues found in production or by customers and contribute to permanent solutions.
Own Your Projects:
Independently manage the technical execution, scheduling, and cost considerations for your test development and support projects based on defined requirements.
What You'll Bring to the Table
Required:
Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering (BSEE) or a closely related field.
4+ years of direct experience in designing, developing, and implementing test solutions for analog and mixed-signal products.
Strong foundational knowledge of analog and digital circuit design, especially as it applies to test fixtures and device interfaces.
Proficiency in a relevant programming language for test automation (e.g., LabVIEW, Python, C#, C++).
Hands-on experience using and controlling test equipment like DMMs, oscilloscopes, power supplies, and function generators.
Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills, with a detail-oriented mindset.
Strong communication and documentation skills.
Preferred:
Experience in a customer-facing technical support or applications engineering role is a significant plus.
Familiarity with various communication protocols (SPI, I2C, UART, USB, Ethernet).
Experience with database interaction for test data storage and analysis.
Hands-on mechanical aptitude or CAD experience for designing enclosures and fixtures.
Why You'll Love Working at Dataforth
Critical Impact:
Play a vital role in guaranteeing the quality and reliability of globally recognized industrial products.
End-to-End Visibility:
See your test systems in action and collaborate directly with the production team at our integrated, on-site manufacturing facility.
A True Full-Spectrum Role:
Engage your skills across the entire product lifecycle, from new product introduction to ensuring customer success in the field.
Work-Life Balance:
Enjoy flexible work hours in a supportive, team-oriented environment.
Invest in Your Future:
Benefit from profit sharing, a 401k plan with company match, and tuition reimbursement.
Comprehensive Benefits:
Access competitive medical, dental, and vision insurance.
Relocation Support:
Assistance is available for qualified candidates moving to the Tucson area.
Ready to Build the Foundation of Quality at Dataforth?
If you are a detail-oriented engineer who is passionate about creating effective test solutions and ensuring customer success, we want to hear from you! Apply today to join a company where your contributions directly ensure product excellence.
Dataforth is an equal opportunity employer & supports a diverse and inclusive work environment. The opportunity
We're looking for a mid-level to senior Full Stack Engineer to build the software that powers materials discovery, from the interfaces scientists use down to the services and data models behind them.
Reporting to the Director of Digital Experience and work closely with the rest of the software engineering team, most of your time will be spent on the frontend: crafting the interfaces scientists and engineers use to navigate vast datasets, turn dense experimental results into charts and interactive graphics they can actually reason about, interact with AI agents, and monitor autonomous lab experiments, all in real time. But we want you to be able to ship a feature end to end. In practice that means adding an RPC to Cortex (our Go backend), evolving the protobuf schema that Cortex shares with every client, and updating the data model in MongoDB, without waiting in line behind a specific backend engineer.
This is not a design role, but you'll collaborate closely with product managers and designers to translate research workflows into intuitive, performant interfaces.
What you'll do
Frontend
Build and maintain complex, data-rich web applications using Svelte and SvelteKit
Implement high-fidelity UI from Figma designs with meticulous attention to detail
Build data visualizations for scientific research and analysis
Architect performant frontend systems that handle async data loading, real-time reactivity, and large-scale state management
Integrate frontend experiences with AI agent capabilities (tool calls, streaming responses, etc.)
Backend and data
Extend Cortex, our Go backend, with new RPC endpoints and business logic, including server-streaming endpoints that push live lab state to the UI as experiments run
Design and evolve the protobuf schemas that define the contract between the backend and every client, keeping changes backward-compatible as generated code lands in TypeScript, Go, and Python
Model and update data in MongoDB: document schemas, indexes, and versioned migrations run against production data
Own features end to end, from schema through service, API, and UI, rather than handing off at the API boundary
Across the stack
Write automated tests on both sides of the API and contribute to CI/CD pipelines
Required qualifications
Core frontend expertise
At least 4 years of professional experience with TypeScript, HTML, and CSS (ideally Tailwind), with a solid grasp of responsive and mobile-first design
Strong experience with modern frontend frameworks and reactive state management (Svelte/SvelteKit preferred; React or Vue acceptable if eager to learn Svelte)
Comfortable with modern build tooling (Vite, ESBuild, Rollup), Node.js, debugging, and performant frontend architecture (async data loading, security, Sentry)
Hands-on data visualization experience, ideally with D3 or low-level SVG/canvas graphics for custom scientific charts
Backend and data fundamentals
Professional experience writing server-side code in a statically typed, compiled language (Go preferred; Java, C#, Rust, or C++ acceptable) and operating in polyglot monorepos
Experience designing and evolving API contracts (gRPC and Protocol Buffers preferred; REST or GraphQL acceptable)
Working knowledge of databases, data modeling, index query performance, and running production data migrations (MongoDB or document stores preferred)
Communication and collaboration
Clear, precise communicator, especially when working across disciplines
Comfortable operating without a hard frontend/backend boundary: you pick up whichever layer the feature needs, and you know when to pull in a specialist
We actively use AI-assisted development and expect engineers to find their own productive workflows with these tools
Pluses
Rendering large datasets without dropping frames: canvas-backed charts, virtualized tables and lists, or moving compute off the main thread with Web Workers
Familiarity with agentic systems (prompting, tool calls, MCP) or AI-frontend integration (e.g. Vercel AI SDK)
Experience delivering real-time data to clients: server-streaming RPCs, WebSockets, SSE, or database change streams
Testing experience: Playwright, Vitest, API mocking, linters and formatters
Observability practice: OpenTelemetry traces, metrics, and structured logs, or an equivalent
Advanced browser APIs such as the History API and structured concurrency in the browser
CI/CD for build and test pipelines (we use self-hosted GitLab CI)
What we offer
Work closely with a team on the cutting edge of AI research
A mission: an opportunity to fundamentally change the way humanity makes progress through materials science discovery

Every engineer eventually finds out which side of the galaxy they are on.
One side is the Empire. Enormous. Gleaming. Impossible to steer. You get a badge, a bay, a ticket queue and a performance cycle. Somewhere above you, eleven levels of command decide what ships. Your code is excellent and almost nobody sees it. The catering is genuinely very good.
The other side is a small crew in a fast ship, flying straight at something that everyone said could not be done.
This is the small crew.
The mission
Imagine a machine that understands taste. Not in the vague marketing sense, in the working sense. A system that learns what a company looks like, sounds like and feels like, then produces world class creative work on its own, at a volume no human studio could match, without losing the thing that made it good in the first place.
That is what this team is building. AI plus creative, pointed at one of the last genuinely human jobs anyone thought was safe. They already do it for customers you would recognise. The next chapter is turning that into a product that anyone can pick up and use, and that is the part you are being hired for.
The founders are the interesting bit. One trained as an artist before switching to computer science. The other has been writing code for more than a decade. They argue about frame timing and system design in the same conversation. Craft is not a tax on velocity here, it is the whole point.
What you will actually build
You are one of the first engineers in. There is no platform team to hand the hard half to, and no design system waiting for you. You build the thing, end to end.
The interface.
React and Next.js. This is a creative product, so the interface is the product. Motion, latency, feel, the 4px that is wrong. A CTO who came out of art school will notice, and will say so.
The backend.
Node, the app layer, workspaces, state, the API the whole self serve product runs on.
The generation layer.
Python. Model orchestration, prompt and scene construction, assembly, and the evaluation logic that catches a bad output before a customer ever sees it.
The agents.
LLM powered agents and agent architectures. The system has to plan the work, not just render it. Multi step reasoning, tool use, branching, retries, guardrails, and the unglamorous engineering that makes an autonomous pipeline survive contact with reality.
The infrastructure.
Long running jobs, queues, media processing, storage, delivery, and cost per run. Generation is slow, expensive and fails in creative ways. Someone owns the difference between a forty second wait and a four minute one. That someone is you.
If human in the loop or preference learning is in your background, bring it up early. Teaching a system what good looks like is the core problem here, not a side quest.
"The Force will be with you. Always."
Obi-Wan Kenobi, Star Wars
Who this is for
Zero to three years as a full stack engineer, and they mean it. This is not a disguised staff role wearing a founding title. What they are buying is speed, taste and the nerve to own a surface with no map.
You will fit if:
Python and JavaScript are both genuinely yours, React and Next.js specifically
You have shipped production web applications end to end, front, back and infrastructure
You have been a founder, a founding engineer, or employee number small at a startup where your job description changed monthly
You have spent time somewhere that takes creative tools or generative AI seriously, the design led product companies and the frontier labs alike
You have built LLM powered things that real people used, not demos
You can defend a technical decision under pressure, and tell a founder they are wrong when they are wrong
You make things outside of work. Design, film, music, art, weird side projects. It does not have to be professional. It counts more than you think
Selective programs like Contrary, Neo Scholars or KP Fellows are a strong signal, not a requirement.
Who this is not for
If your entire career is a straight line through the biggest companies in tech, with no startup chapter anywhere and nothing you built yourself, this will not work. Not because that work is easy, but because this job has no scaffolding, no roadmap handed down and no one to escalate to at 11pm.
Coming from a giant is fine. Having only ever been inside one is the problem. Big tech plus a company you started, plus something you shipped alone that people actually used, is a very strong profile here.
The deal
$250,000 to $275,000 base
, set by timing and profile
Founding equity
, materially larger the earlier you land
Lunch and dinner daily
Five days a week in the San Francisco office.
In the room, with the founders, every day. If that sounds like a cost rather than the point, this is not your ship
US work authorization required.
No visa sponsorship of any kind, so US citizens and Green Card holders only
Multiple hires being made on this search
Boarding
The Empire is hiring too. Better parking, clearer ladder, nobody remembers your name.
Send your CV, your GitHub, and whatever you have made that you are quietly proud of.
Keiran Hathorn, Big Wave Digital
keiran@bigwavedigital.com.au
Founding Engineer | AI + Creative | San Francisco | $250K to $275K + Founding Equity

Earn your master's degree while building real-world open source software.
Kitware's Open Source Software Technology Program (OSTP) is a full-time position for talented and curious new Computer Science and Computer Engineering graduates, offering an opportunity to launch their careers while earning a master's degree in Computer Science.
You'll work on real-world open source software projects, develop your technical and leadership skills, and complete your graduate education - all while earning a competitive salary.
You'll gain experience developing innovative software with applications across areas such as computer vision, scientific computing, data and analytics, medical computing, and software solutions. Along the way, you'll learn not only how to build and maintain powerful open source platforms, but also how successful technical projects are led, funded, and sustained.
How It Works
OSTP Software Developers join Kitware as
full-time, permanent employees from day one
. The program is designed to combine professional software development experience with graduate study, with the master's degree typically completed over a three-year period.
Throughout that time, you'll work on-site at Kitware's Clifton Park, NY headquarters while completing your master's coursework. Your work schedule is designed with the demands of graduate study in mind, with flexibility during the academic year to balance your Kitware responsibilities and coursework. During the summer and other academic breaks, you'll have greater availability to focus on your work at Kitware.
Kitware covers
100% of educational expenses for your master's degree
. By the time you complete your degree, you'll have also gained approximately three years of professional experience developing open source software. And because OSTP is a permanent position - not a three-year appointment - we hope earning your master's degree will be one milestone in a long-term career with Kitware.
What You'll Do
Work on a variety of real-world open source software projects.
Develop software with applications across computer vision, scientific computing, data and analytics, medical computing, and other technical areas.
Build a deep understanding of what it takes to create, maintain, and grow powerful open source software platforms.
Learn open source software development processes and best practices.
Develop technical and business knowledge that can prepare you for future leadership opportunities.
Learn the fundamentals of project leadership.
Gain exposure to how funding is acquired to support the development and growth of open source platforms.
Complete your master's degree in Computer Science while gaining professional software development experience.
What We're Looking For
This position is specifically designed for recent graduates who are ready to continue their education while beginning their professional software development careers.
Be completing a bachelor's degree in Computer Science or Computer Engineering in Spring 2027. December 2026 graduates will also be considered.
Have demonstrable programming experience through undergraduate projects, internships, or similar experience.
Have experience programming in both C++ and Python.
Have strong communication skills.
Be willing and able to meet the program's on-site work requirements in Clifton Park, NY.
Due to contractual requirements, this position requires U.S. citizenship and a willingness and ability to obtain and maintain a security clearance.
Employment visa sponsorship is not offered for this position.
Preferred Qualifications
Existing experience with open source software development.
$75,000 - $85,000 a year
Why Kitware?
Kitware is a research and development software company working to advance science, make a positive impact, and share our results. Our work contributes to areas including healthcare, national security, scientific discovery, and advanced computing, and our customers and collaborators include government organizations, national laboratories, leading universities, medical device manufacturers, technology companies, and other organizations around the world.
Open source software is central to how we work. For someone beginning a career in software development, that means an opportunity to learn by contributing to real software, working alongside experienced researchers and developers, and seeing how collaborative software projects grow from technical ideas into platforms used by others.
We're also
100% employee-owned through an Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP)
. Eligible employees have the opportunity to share in the value they help create, giving our people a meaningful stake in Kitware's long-term success.
Our employees enjoy a collaborative work environment, flexibility in their assignments, significant independence, and the opportunity to take ownership of their work.
Benefits Include
Six weeks of paid time off
Flexible working hours
Competitive compensation
401(k)
Health and life insurance
Short- and long-term disability insurance
Free coffee, drinks, and snacks
For more information on our benefit offerings please visit: https://www.kitware.com/careers/.
Living & Working in New York's Capital Region
The OSTP is offered exclusively at Kitware's Clifton Park, NY headquarters, putting you in the heart of New York's Capital Region.
This area offers the conveniences and culture of city living with a distinctly small-town feel. From Broadway shows and outdoor concerts to a strong local dining scene, there’s plenty to do without the pace of a larger metropolitan area.
What really sets the region apart is its access to the outdoors. With an abundance of parks, lakes, nature preserves, and trails, outdoor recreation is part of life year-round from hiking and boating in the warmer months to skiing and snowshoeing in the winter.
Kitware's Clifton Park headquarters includes collaborative gathering spaces, an oversized kitchen stocked with beverages and snacks, and an expansive outdoor patio.

About ITradeNetwork
At iTradeNetwork, we provide advanced supply chain software and insights tailored to the food & beverage industry. Our mission is clear and ambitious:
To feed the world.
From the start, we’ve been dedicated to tackling the most pressing challenges within food and beverage supply chains, delivering innovative solutions and expert support that make a measurable impact.
Our cutting-edge technology helps businesses streamline complex procurement and fulfillment processes, minimize food waste, optimize inventory, manage compliance risk, and scale profitably. We’re proud to serve an elite customer base, including 13 of the top 25 North American grocers, 8 of the top 10 foodservice distributors, and 8 of the top 10 global food and beverage manufacturers.
Today, we're building an AI-first company — meaning AI isn't a feature we bolt on, it's the foundation for how we design products, make decisions, and ship software. Cerena is proof of that in action: powered by the most connected supply chain network in food and beverage, iTradeNetwork's Solution Suite replaces error-prone manual workflows with faster, smarter tools — driving real results for our customers, and ultimately, for the consumers who depend on them.
iTradeNetwork's Leadership Principles
iTradeNetwork’s purpose is to feed the world — and everything we do is guided by the principles below. Every team member is expected to embody and champion these principles across the organization.
Bias for Action
We value speed and avoid analysis paralysis. We develop conviction, make informed decisions quickly, and take calculated risks to maintain momentum — knowing that swift progress is essential for innovation and growth.
Customer Obsession
We work relentlessly to delight our customers. We work backward from their needs to solve pain points and create solutions that surprise and earn their loyalty. We obsess over customers, not competitors.
Data & Metrics Driven
We operate with facts, not opinions. We dive deep into data and use metrics to measure progress, ground every decision in rigorous analysis, and push for clarity and measurable outcomes.
Raise the Bar
We continuously push for improvement — in ourselves, our teams, and the company. We hire and develop exceptional talent, setting ever-higher standards that elevate performance and drive excellence.
Operational Excellence Through Process
We build lasting processes that optimize for efficiency. By developing, testing, and documenting each process, we create consistency and scale through automation, enabling continuous improvement across the business.
Ownership Mindset
We take responsibility for our work and aim for long-term success. We use resources wisely, stay accountable, and roll up our sleeves to get things done — no task is beneath us.
Earn Trust
We build trust through integrity, transparency, and mutual respect. We communicate openly, own our mistakes, listen actively, and remain open to feedback as an opportunity for growth.
Job Summary
We are building an AI-first company — which means AI isn’t a feature we bolt on; it’s the foundation of how we design products, make decisions, and ship software. As an Associate AI/ML Full Stack Developer, you’ll be on the front lines of that mission: building intelligent, production-ready applications that put machine learning at the core of the user experience.
This is a role for someone who wants to grow fast. You’ll work alongside experienced engineers and data scientists on real problems, ship code that matters, and develop deep expertise at the intersection of AI/ML and full stack development — all in service of one of the most consequential industries in the world.
Key Responsibilities
Build and ship AI-powered full stack applications — from model integration to user-facing interfaces — using modern frameworks and cloud-native infrastructure.
Partner with data scientists to bring ML models into production: wrapping them in APIs, optimizing inference pipelines, and monitoring performance in live environments.
Own end-to-end data pipelines that support model training, validation, and deployment workflows.
Develop frontend experiences (React or similar) that surface AI-driven insights in intuitive, responsive interfaces.
Contribute to backend services and microservices that power model serving, data ingestion, and business logic.
Participate in code reviews and collaborative design discussions — learning from senior engineers while sharing your own perspective.
Stay current with the AI/ML landscape: new architectures, tooling, and frameworks move fast, and so do we.
Required
What you’ll need:
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science or a related technical field (or equivalent practical experience).
Solid grounding in data structures, algorithms, and object-oriented programming.
Understanding of core AI/ML concepts: supervised and unsupervised learning, neural networks, model evaluation.
Proficiency in at least one backend language — Python strongly preferred given its centrality to the ML ecosystem.
Hands-on experience with web development (React, Angular, or comparable framework).
Comfort with both SQL and NoSQL databases.
A problem-solving mindset and genuine curiosity about how AI can change the way software works.
Nice To Have
Experience with Python ML libraries: TensorFlow, PyTorch, or Scikit-learn.
Familiarity with cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, or Azure) and deploying ML workloads in the cloud.
Exposure to LLM APIs, prompt engineering, or retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) patterns.
Knowledge of MLOps tooling: experiment tracking, model registries, CI/CD for ML pipelines.
Project or coursework experience building AI/ML applications end-to-end.
Who You Are
You think AI-first — when approaching a problem, your instinct is to ask how intelligence can be built into the solution, not added as an afterthought.
You move fast and learn faster. You’re comfortable with ambiguity and excited by the pace of change in the AI space.

Description
Imagine running search and analytics at any scale without thinking about clusters, capacity, or version upgrades. Where your queries return in milliseconds whether you're indexing a thousand documents or a hundred billion. Where the platform scales, heals, and secures itself so your team can focus on the questions, not the infrastructure.
That's what we build.
Amazon OpenSearch Service is the fully managed and Serverless AWS service that lets customers deploy, operate, and scale OpenSearch for log analytics, full-text search, application monitoring, observability, and AI-powered retrieval. We serve hundreds of thousands of customers running mission-critical workloads across every AWS region, and we are part of the AWS Database and Analytics organization.
Come join the OpenSearch Control Plane team. We are responsible for a service that:
Reliably manages a large fleet of cloud-native OpenSearch clusters and collections, freeing customers from sizing, scaling, and patching decisions
Guarantees high availability and durability for mission-critical search and observability workloads at the scale of the most demanding internet businesses
Orchestrates and automates the complete lifecycle of an OpenSearch cluster or collection — from creation through scale-up, scale-out, upgrade, replication, and fail-over
The OpenSearch control plane is not just any distributed system. It orchestrates a fleet of clusters across every AWS region, detects and recovers from node failures in seconds, and serves workloads that span petabytes of customer data. Most recently, we launched **OpenSearch Serverless NextGen** — delivering ultra-fast collection provisioning and true scale-to-zero capacity, so customers pay only for what they use and get a working environment in seconds rather than minutes. We are not done; this is one of many investments raising the bar for what customers can expect from a managed search service.
OpenSearch itself is a community-driven, Apache 2.0–licensed open-source search and analytics suite built on Apache Lucene. Since launching in July 2021, the project has delivered multiple major and minor releases advancing core search, vector search, and analytics. Our next phase focuses on transforming OpenSearch into an intelligent retrieval engine — one that meets the evolving needs of customers running search, analytics, and AI-powered workloads across structured, unstructured, and multi-modal data.
We work in Java, Rust, Python, and Go. We contribute upstream to OpenSearch and Apache Lucene. We are customer-obsessed, operate with the entrepreneurial pace of a startup inside one of the world's largest cloud providers, and value strong intuition backed by metrics.
Operations is core engineering on this team, not overhead.** Engineers operate what they build, and we treat customer-impacting incidents with the same engineering rigor we apply to feature work. Reliability and Static Stability is a forcing function for design, not a phase after launch.

About The Role
We're hiring an experienced ML engineer to work on the models that see. You'll own problems end to end: deciding what data you need, getting it, training on it, proving the result is actually better, and getting it running inside the vehicle's constraints.
The problems you'd be working on
Rather than a list of responsibilities, here's what the team is actually chewing on:
A model that's two points better offline can be worse on the road.
Aggregate benchmark numbers hide the failures that matter — the rare scene, the unusual agent, the bad lighting. Building evaluation that predicts on-road behaviour, and knowing when to distrust your own metric, is a bigger part of this job than architecture search.
We generate far more data than anyone can look at.
The interesting frames are a vanishingly small fraction of what the fleet records. Finding them, deciding what's worth labelling, and keeping the training set honest as the distribution shifts is continuous work, not a one-time setup.
The vehicle's compute budget is fixed and already full.
Everything you add competes with everything already running. You'll be making concrete trades between accuracy, latency, and memory, and defending them.
Modern architectures keep changing what's possible.
Transformers and multimodal models opened up approaches that weren't available two years ago. Part of the job is reading what's coming out, judging honestly whether it applies to our problem, and being willing to conclude that it doesn't.
Nothing ships alone.
Your model's output is someone else's input. You'll work directly with the planning, infrastructure, and vehicle software teams, and the handoffs are where most of the real difficulty lives.
What we're looking for
You've shipped a neural network, not just trained one. At least three years taking models from data collection through training to something that ran in production or on real hardware, and stayed working.
Real depth in one modern ML area — computer vision, large language models, or generative modelling. We'd rather see one domain you know properly than six you've touched.
Python and a modern deep learning framework, fluently, as your daily working environment.
Enough C++ to be useful. Inference runs in C++ on the vehicle. You don't need to be a C++ specialist, but you need to be able to read the code your model runs inside and work with the engineers who own it.
Comfort with large-scale data tooling and SQL — you can get your own data without waiting on someone else.
You read papers and can tell which ones matter. Most don't.
You can explain a technical trade-off to someone who doesn't share your background and hold your position when it's the right call.
Things that would stand out
You've made a model meaningfully faster on target hardware and can explain what you gave up to get there.
You've worked on ML for autonomous vehicles or robotics before, and know how different the failure modes are from a benchmark.
Published work or open-source contributions we can actually read — send us a link and we'll read it.
A track record of setting a direction and following it through without needing to be steered.

About The Role
Vercel builds and maintains a broad portfolio of open source projects that power the modern web, running in millions of applications. Your primary focus will be
Turborepo, Nuxt, Svelte/SvelteKit, SWR, Workflow, and Nitro
. A single structural fix at the framework level protects every one of those applications at once, which makes this one of the highest-leverage security roles at the company.
We're looking for a security engineer who loves finding a whole class of vulnerability and eliminating it in one move, not someone who's satisfied filing one bug at a time. You'll run deep security assessments of framework internals (routing, middleware, caching, server actions, the build pipeline), find the systemic patterns that produce entire families of bugs, and drive the framework-level fixes and design changes that remove them permanently. You'll also own how these projects handle externally reported vulnerabilities, coordinated disclosure, and CVEs, working directly with maintainers and the open source security community. This includes hands-on ownership of Vercel's open source bug bounty program for these projects: triaging incoming reports, validating and reproducing findings, and driving fixes with the right maintainers.
What you will do
Hunt for vulnerability classes, not individual bugs: Run deep security assessments of framework internals (routing, middleware, caching, data fetching, server actions/RSC boundaries, build tooling) to find the systemic design patterns that produce whole families of issues.
Drive root-cause framework fixes: Push design changes upstream that eliminate a category of vulnerability across every application built on the framework, rather than patching individual instances as they're reported.
Own vulnerability disclosure and CVEs: Triage security reports from the community and researchers across Turborepo, Nuxt, Svelte/SvelteKit, SWR, Workflow, Nitro, and other maintained OSS projects. Coordinate embargoed fixes, write and publish advisories, and manage the CVE/CNA process end to end.
Run the OSS bug bounty program for these projects: Own triage and validation of incoming reports to Vercel's open source bug bounty program for Turborepo, Nuxt, Svelte/SvelteKit, SWR, Workflow, and Nitro. Reproduce findings, assess severity, and coordinate fixes with the right maintainers and researchers.
Get security into design early: Partner with framework maintainers and core teams during RFCs and design review, so new features ship with security considered from the first draft, not bolted on after a report comes in.
Build preventive tooling: Contribute linters, codemods, and CI checks that catch regressions of previously-fixed vulnerability classes before they land again.
Own supply chain security for these projects: Harden how dependencies, releases, and published packages for Turborepo, Nuxt, Svelte/SvelteKit, SWR, Workflow, and Nitro are built, signed, and distributed. As more contributions and dependency updates are generated or assisted by AI agents, build the review and provenance practices that keep that increased volume safe.
Work with the community, not around it: Engage directly with maintainers, contributors, and external researchers as peers. Bring pragmatic security recommendations to project discussions in a way that respects how these projects actually get built, and represent Vercel in coordinated disclosure norms and working groups when an issue spans multiple ecosystems.
About You
You've actually used or broken these frameworks: You've built real things with Turborepo, Nuxt, Svelte/SvelteKit, SWR, Workflow, or Nitro (or closely comparable projects), or you've found and reported security issues in them. This is a hard requirement, not a nice-to-have: we need someone who understands what these projects actually do and how they're actually used, not a generalist parachuting in.
You have a deep appreciation and respect for open source work: You understand that these are community projects with maintainers, contributors, and users who care deeply about them, and you treat that with the seriousness it deserves. You're not here to slow the project down with process for its own sake.
4+ years in security engineering, ideally with real hands-on open source contribution experience. You've actually sent PRs to projects like these, not just filed issues against them.
You're energized by root cause, not remediation count: Finding the one design flaw that kills fifty potential bugs is more satisfying to you than closing fifty tickets one at a time.
You can read framework internals, not just application code: Strong JavaScript/TypeScript fundamentals and genuine familiarity with how modern meta-frameworks work under the hood (routing, SSR/RSC, middleware, bundling/build systems).
Pragmatic, not theoretical: You can weigh real-world risk against maintainer and community bandwidth, and land on security improvements that actually ship, rather than the theoretically ideal fix that never gets merged.
Vulnerability research chops: Experience with structured security assessment methodology and coordinated/responsible disclosure processes, including handling embargoes and writing clear adviso

Configurator ownership —

Stability —
Diagnose and resolve rendering, texture and canvas issues, including browser memory leaks and WebGL context loss.
Technical leadership —
Lead architecture, code review and feature delivery for real-time product personalization.

Recipe → SAP —
Design and maintain the mapping from a customer’s 3D “recipe” to a valid, orderable outcome in SAP S/4HANA — resolving each configuration to the correct material / SKU, Bill of Materials and price, using SAP variant configuration / configurable materials and made-to-order flows as applicable.

Keep the configurator’s variant / option matrix in sync with master data governed in Centric PLM and Precisely EnterWorks, so options, prices and availability stay accurate.

Availability logic —
Implement made-to-order availability and lead-time logic in the configuration experience (finished-product availability and lead times, not raw-material inventory).

Data contracts —
Establish stable data contracts (JSON payloads, catalog indexes, option and price models) between the front end and back-end systems.
Accuracy —
Ensure price and SKU accuracy end to end, so the configured price and product match what is ordered, invoiced and manufactured.

Implement ICC-based color management so on-screen color matches the manufactured product across materials, thread, print and engraving.

Implement personalization safeguards — profanity and trademark / brand moderation on custom text and uploaded logos.

Asset workflows —
Partner with 3D design / asset teams (internal or agency) to translate high-fidelity CAD / mesh assets into optimized web assets, communicating payload, texture and performance constraints. Deep 3D artistry and shader authoring are a plus, not the primary function of this role.
Versioning —
Maintain versioned asset and configuration pipelines with clear release control.

Define and monitor performance and quality metrics (Core Web Vitals, frame rate, error rates, uptime) and act on regressions.

Ensure configurator experiences meet accessibility standards (WCAG 2.x).

Drive reusability through modular components, presets and templates; support documentation, onboarding and engineering standards.

Service and Support
• Perform regular inspections, maintenance, and software updates of control systems
• Identify and address system malfunctions or inefficiencies promptly
• Implement system upgrades and enhancements to improve efficiency and performance
• Continuously monitor service and support channels, including phone lines, email, chat, and ticketing systems
• Track service metrics, performance indicators, and key performance indicators (KPIs) to identify issues and trends

• Develop incident response protocols and ensure they are followed
Instrumentation & Electrical Design
• Create instrument lists by examining P&ID drawings
• Compile submittal and procurement documentation for controls and instrument hardware
• Provide technical support for panel fabrication technicians
• Inspect completed control enclosures

• Assemble development system using project hardware and computers
• Configure user interface and HMI screens

• Draft system documentation from templates
• Assist is customer demonstrations and acceptance testing
• Configure networks to interface with equipment.

• Install project software and configuration onto site systems
• Participate in point-to-point loop checks
• Perform instrumentation and software calibration and tuning
• Participate in functional tests of all systems
• Troubleshoot installation discrepancies
• Program field modifications as required
• Assist with developing commissioning test plans and documentation updates/redlines
• Assist with developing training documentation/presentation on operations and maintenance of system

• Requires on-call rotation to address critical system issues outside regular working hours.

• Proven track record as a Service Specialist and experience in service and support operations in a 24/7 environment.
• Associate’s Degree in approved mechanical or electrical program, or proper background as determined by interview
Technical Experience (One or more of the following technologies)
• Controls Experience: Tridium: Niagara N4
• Distech: Experience with BACnet and LON Distech controllers, Eclypse Controllers
• Johnson Controls: Facility Explorer or Metasys controllers
• Siemens: Experienced with Apogee (PXC), Talon Controllers, DXR controllers, Desigo CC or Insight
• Rockwell: FactoryTalk Suite, RS Logix/Studio 5000, familiarity with PlantPAx DCS
• Other useful technologies include: Scripting languages (VBA, Python, etc.)
• Knowledge of Kepware OPC server, ThinManager, VMware is preferred.
HVAC Experience Preferred:
• Basic understanding of HVAC systems in large building automation systems.
• Understanding of sequence of operations and P&IDs for HVAC and plant utilities.
• Experience with functional testing, including the ability to create, maintain, and execute test plans.
• Experience with specifying instrumentation and control valves for HVAC systems

Our team in Amazon Robotics builds robotic systems that perform contact-rich manipulation tasks safely and reliably in complex, unstructured environments — at Amazon scale. Job ID: 115202
The Leonardo DRS Airborne and Intelligence Systems business is a global leader and strategic partner committed to delivering world-class, full life-cycle defense and intelligence products that protect the security of our nation and our allies. From air combat training to state-of-the-art electronic warfare systems, our technology is deployed by virtually all U.S. military and government agencies around the world.
This is a hybrid position open to candidates who reside in or near Beavercreek, Ohio; Frederick, Maryland; or Fort Walton Beach, Florida.
Job Summary
Own the engine room the whole AI function runs on.
We've used AI before, now we treat it as a first-class citizen at Airborne & Intelligence Systems (AIS). We build and deploy AI across signals intelligence, electronic warfare, air combat training, and the mission systems that connect them. This work shows up on our floor, in the field, and on the company's P&L, while meeting the demanding standards of our defense and commercial customers. If you want your work and your talent to count, this is the place.
AI has to run on real hardware, and someone has to own it. That’s you. You stand up our own AI servers from bare metal — open-weight models, high-performance GPU hosting — keep them running, keep them secure, and fix them when they break. You also build and deploy AI systems on the corporate secure cloud as a developer.
This is a build-and-run role: you don’t just stand infrastructure up; you operate it so that what you build keeps working without you in the room. For our own hosting, you are the platform team. On the corporate cloud you are a developer, not the administrator. Corporate IT owns the cloud platform itself (provisioning, networking, identity, patching). You build on it; you don’t run it, and you don’t build a competing platform. If that boundary chafes, this isn’t the seat; if it reads as clarity, keep going.
At the heart of this function is a proprietary platform, the encoded way this business does AI. It takes any employee from a rough idea to a governed, well-formed use case, checks it against the rules, and prepares a recommendation a human decision-maker rules on. You don't just use it; you also build it. You build and host the platform itself, along with the self-serve tools that carry it to the wider workforce. The system everyone else uses runs on infrastructure that you own and operate.
This is a high impact, founding individual-contributor seat within the technical core of AI Excellence function with meaningful end to end work ownership. You report directly to top leadership of the function giving you outsize visibility, opportunity for personal growth and direct line to impact. Your peers will be AI leads for Solutions & Delivery/Evaluation & Measurement.
Job Responsibilities
Primary & Essential Accountabilities
Stand up local AI hosting. Model serving, MLOps, and server-level administration for on-premises, self-hosted, and air-gapped environments — setup through sustainment.
Deploy on the secure cloud. Develop, integrate, and ship AI systems on the corporate GCC High environment as a developer.
Own security and accreditation engineering. Get our hosting to an authorization-to-operate; partner with the security office; flag capabilities that can’t get there.
Instrument everything you run. Tracing, telemetry, and observability are part of the build, not an afterthought — you’ll know it’s failing before a user calls.
Build the tooling everyone uses. Host the shared AI platform tooling and the self-serve tools that reach the wider workforce.
Ship only what’s been cleared. You deploy; a separate teammate runs the quality gate. You are the builder, not the grader of your own work
Qualifications
5+ years in infrastructure, platform, or site-reliability engineering (regardless of total years exp), including 3+ years in MLOps or model serving, with recent hands-on self-hosted or LLM-inference/training/tuning work.
A hands-on record of standing up model-serving or hosting in production and then operating it — an infrastructure builder, not just a platform user. Expect to walk us through what you built, what broke at 2 a.m., how you knew, and what you changed so it wouldn’t again.
At least one environment stood up from the first server, with no inherited platform — and it outlived your day-to-day involvement because you documented and hardened it.
Server-level system administration and security engineering for self-hosted and air-gapped systems.
Cloud development capability (developer, not just user); working fluency with open-weight models, quantization, and sanctioned endpoints.
Bachelor’s degree and 5 years experience or equivalent combination of both. Engineering, Computer Science, Data Science, or a related technical field is preferred.
Five years of relevant experience (or an equivalent combination of experience and training that provides the required knowledge, skills, and abilities.
Proficient technical expertise with demonstrated application.
Excellent interpersonal, leadership, negotiation, communication and writing skills.
Preferred Qualifications
Carried a system through security accreditation (ATO / CMMC / FedRAMP) as the ISSO or security lead.
Deep modern inference optimization: quantization, multi-model VRAM budgeting, serving-stack tuning (vLLM or equivalent).
GovCloud / GCC High / DoD environment familiarity.
Experience hosting coding-assistant or IDE-service model sets.
Active security clearance

Full time, six months, $65,000 ($130,000 annualized). I
3% of children are autistic. 30% of them at age 9 remain minimally verbal: a handful of single words, never put together into a sentence.
Does that evoke something in you beyond the number? A personal connection, or some other experience that lets you feel the texture of the problem?
If so, read on.
The Kasari Lab at UCLA, one of the top autism research groups in the world, has developed a play-based intervention that helps minimally verbal autistic children. Over 24 weeks, many make real gains in communication and social connection.
The intervention involves a combination of assistive tech setup and play improvisation that makes it challenging to deliver. It is not standard practice.
You would be making Visual Play, a delightful app that takes pieces of this intervention, and others, and makes them easier for regular clinicians to do. Embedded in the lab from Day 1, paired with an implementation lead who spends their weeks with clinicians, you would create something a clinician could use while playing with a child.
There's nothing harder than child's play. Our job is to make it easier.
Visual Play is funded by an NIH SBIR award to SKIES, a small Pasadena company started by Caltech alums that makes Visual Choices, one of the most-used communication apps for early communicators. This is a six-month Phase I. If the prototype works, Phase II follows, and so does the product. The goal is to improve autism intervention in Los Angeles, and beyond.
An Ideal Candidate
is comfortable being close to, and taking feedback from, researchers and clinicians;
has shipped real native iOS apps;
uses AI as a force multiplier, but understands the code it produces and is not dependent on it;
builds large and complex, yet maintainable, systems;
is resourceful, motivated, and tenacious;
is a calm, respectful presence in a research lab.
Full time, six months, $65,000 ($130,000 annualized). In person at UCLA. Starting as soon as we find the right person. Interested? Contact julius@skieslearn.com.

A fast-growing, well-funded consumer technology company in San Francisco is looking for an exceptional iOS Engineer to join a small, highly technical engineering team building the next generation of intelligent, connected consumer products.
About the Role
This is not a traditional mobile-app role. The iOS application sits at the heart of the product experience, connecting directly with physical devices and providing the primary interface through which users interact with them. You’ll work across native iOS, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi connectivity, real-time data, device state and AI-enabled features, partnering closely with hardware, firmware, backend and machine-learning engineers. The team is intentionally small, highly experienced and deeply product-focused. Engineers have significant ownership and are expected to take features from initial architecture all the way through development, testing and release.
Responsibilities
What You’ll Be Working On
You’ll help design and build a sophisticated native iOS application that communicates directly with connected hardware. Your work will include:
Building reliable Bluetooth Low Energy and Wi-Fi pairing experiences
Managing device connection, reconnection and background connectivity
Developing real-time interfaces that respond instantly to changing device state
Working with streaming data between hardware, mobile and cloud systems
Supporting firmware updates delivered through the mobile application
Designing robust device-state and synchronisation architecture
Handling offline, degraded and unreliable connectivity gracefully
Building AI-enabled product experiences involving both local and cloud processing
Working with iOS background modes, notifications and Bluetooth permissions
Optimising application performance and battery usage
Taking features from technical design through to production and App Store release
This is the kind of environment where you may be sitting with a firmware engineer debugging why a physical device is dropping its connection one minute, then designing a new SwiftUI experience the next.
Qualifications
What We’re Looking For
You’ll need strong commercial experience building and shipping native iOS applications. The quality and complexity of what you have built matters more than an exact number of years.
Required Skills
You should have:
Strong commercial Swift experience
Strong SwiftUI and/or UIKit experience
Experience shipping production iOS applications
Experience with Core Bluetooth and/or real-time data streaming
A strong understanding of iOS architecture and application state
Experience taking features from architecture through implementation, testing and release
Strong debugging and problem-solving skills
Confidence working directly with engineers across different technical disciplines
The ability to work independently without needing heavy process or supervision

Preferred Skills

Connected consumer devices

IoT products

Audio hardware

How should the app recover when a device comes back online?
How do we keep the UI perfectly aligned with the state of a physical device?

Build useful software. Use AI extensively. Keep getting better.
Terros builds software that helps field sales teams manage their work, understand performance, and serve customers more effectively. We’re looking for a resourceful engineer who enjoys solving problems and uses AI to turn ideas into working software.
We care more about what you can build, how you approach unfamiliar problems, and how quickly you learn than where you went to school or which titles you’ve held.
A computer science degree is not required. There is no minimum number of years of professional experience.
Your experience might come from a job, an internship, coursework, freelancing, or something you built yourself. What matters is that you have something concrete to discuss and can explain your contribution.
The role
You’ll work closely with our CTO and engineering team to build features, improve existing software, and solve problems that matter to customers.
AI coding tools will be a regular part of your work. We expect you to use them to explore code, investigate problems, develop solutions, and improve testing. This is primarily a role for
building software with AI
, not researching models or exclusively building AI features.
You don’t need to write every line from memory. You do need to understand the changes you make, investigate unexpected behavior, and check that the result actually works.
Our technology
Terros is built across a modern cloud and mobile stack. Our backend runs primarily on
AWS
, with much of our application and infrastructure code written in
TypeScript
. Our mobile applications are native:
Swift
on iOS and
Kotlin
on Android.
You do not need to be an expert in all three languages when you join, but you should be comfortable learning across the stack and using AI tools to become productive quickly. Experience building on AWS is especially valuable because understanding how cloud services, infrastructure, logs, permissions, queues, databases, and deployed applications fit together is an important part of troubleshooting and shipping software at Terros.
What You’ll Do
Build and improve the product. Turn customer needs into practical features, fix defects, and follow changes through testing and release.
Use AI thoughtfully. Give coding agents useful context, evaluate their suggestions, and recognize when their output needs correction.
Take initiative. Ask why a problem matters, suggest simpler approaches, and identify useful improvements rather than waiting for every step to be prescribed.
Work with the team. Participate in code reviews, communicate progress and uncertainty, ask for help when needed, and apply feedback to your next change.
As you become familiar with the product, you’ll also help troubleshoot customer issues and participate in our engineering support rotation.
What We’re Looking For
Evidence that you can build.
You have created or meaningfully improved something with code. It does not need to be commercially successful, publicly available, or technically elaborate—but you should be able to explain how it works and what you did.
Practical experience with AI coding tools.
You’ve used modern AI coding tools to do more than generate isolated snippets. You can describe how you worked through a real task, what you delegated to AI, what the tools got right or wrong, and how you verified the result. We don’t care which specific tools or models you prefer--we expect them to keep changing.
Curiosity and resourcefulness.
When something is unfamiliar, you investigate, experiment, and ask useful questions. You don’t need to know everything already, but you want to understand more than the immediate answer.
Initiative and follow-through.
You notice problems, propose solutions, and finish agreed work. When you get stuck or discover a risk, you communicate rather than letting it sit.
Openness to feedback.
You can reconsider an approach, explain your reasoning, and improve your work without becoming attached to the first solution.
What You Can Expect
You’ll work on a real product with direct access to the people making technical and product decisions. You’ll receive technical guidance and feedback, with responsibilities matched to your demonstrated ability and increasing as you learn.
We don’t expect you to arrive knowing our entire codebase. We do expect you to take an active role in learning it and become increasingly effective at delivering reliable work.
Location requirement
You must currently live in Southern California and be able to work in person at our Irvine office.
This is not a remote position. We are considering local applicants only, not applicants planning to relocate.
How To Apply
Submit your résumé or a short summary of your experience and answer a few questions about something you’ve built and how you use AI.
Links to a project, repository, demo, or screenshots are welcome but optional. You do not need a public GitHub profile, and you should not share confidential work.
Selected candidates will complete a practical exercise using AI tools. We’re interested in how you investigate, build, verify, and explain your work--not how much code you can write from memory.

AI@HHMI:

This role is part of the AI+CryoET project within AI@HHMI, a multi-institutional project at the intersection of cryo-electron tomography (cryoET), molecular dynamics simulation, and machine learning. The project aims to develop AI methods for mesoscale structural biology, understanding how cellular macromolecules organize into higher-order structures. You will work in a team at Janelia, with experimental and computational collaborators across the Rosen lab (UT Southwestern Medical Center/HHMI), Gouaux lab (Oregon Health and Science University/HHMI), Collepardo-Guevara lab (University of Cambridge), and Villa lab (UC San Diego/HHMI).
